- Exit 0 pass, 1 findings, 2 usage. `--json` prints `{ pass, findings: [{ path, line, rule, message }] }`.

implications.text: The CLI and step.docs.check must apply the same rules (spec §7.2: 'the same rules as sindri docs check'), so the rules move into one shared check rather than being copied.

The existing findings carry rule, item, message, fix and no line; the CLI's JSON needs path and line, so the shared check records the line of a broken link or an unclosed fence, and null where a finding has no line.

`--facts <dir>` reads the Step's inputs from files under <dir> named after the facts (docsScope, workspace), the run-folder convention; the spec's own example passes the run folder (`sindri docs check --facts "$AW_SINDRI_RUN_DIR" --json`). A missing or unreadable fact is a usage error (exit 2), not a finding.
Class local means the verb is resolved in process before any control-plane client is built, so it works with serve down and from an agent session.

items.text: When `sindri docs check --facts <dir>` runs and the facts under <dir> describe a docs change whose paths are all doc paths, whose relative links all resolve and whose markdown all parses, the CLI shall print that the check passed and exit 0.
When the docs change under <dir> holds a path that is neither under the profile's doc globs nor a doc the design names, the CLI shall report a DOCS-PATH-001 finding for that path and exit 1.

When a changed markdown file has a relative link whose target does not exist in the workspace (or climbs out of the repo root), the CLI shall report a DOCS-LINK-001 finding naming the file, the link's line and the target, and exit 1.
When a changed markdown file does not parse (a code fence that is opened and never closed), the CLI shall report a DOCS-MD-001 finding naming the file and the fence's line, and exit 1.

When `--json` is given, the CLI shall print exactly one JSON document `{ pass, findings: [{ path, line, rule, message }] }` on standard output, with `pass` true and `findings` empty on a pass, and the same exit code as the text form.

If `docs check` is called without `--facts <dir>`, with an unknown argument, or with a <dir> that is missing or lacks a readable fact the check needs, then the CLI shall print a usage error naming the problem and exit 2.

implications.text: The CLI and step.docs.check must apply the same rules (spec §7.2: 'the same rules as sindri docs check'), so the rules move into one shared check rather than being copied.

The existing findings carry rule, item, message, fix and no line; the CLI's JSON needs path and line, so the shared check records the line of a broken link or an unclosed fence, and null where a finding has no line.

`--facts <dir>` reads the Step's inputs from files under <dir> named after the facts (docsScope, workspace), the run-folder convention; the spec's own example passes the run folder (`sindri docs check --facts "$AW_SINDRI_RUN_DIR" --json`). A missing or unreadable fact is a usage error (exit 2), not a finding.
Class local means the verb is resolved in process before any control-plane client is built, so it works with serve down and from an agent session.

items.text: When `sindri docs check --facts <dir>` runs and the facts under <dir> describe a docs change whose paths are all doc paths, whose relative links all resolve and whose markdown all parses, the CLI shall print that the check passed and exit 0.
When the docs change under <dir> holds a path that is neither under the profile's doc globs nor a doc the design names, the CLI shall report a DOCS-PATH-001 finding for that path and exit 1.

When a changed markdown file has a relative link whose target does not exist in the workspace (or climbs out of the repo root), the CLI shall report a DOCS-LINK-001 finding naming the file, the link's line and the target, and exit 1.
When a changed markdown file does not parse (a code fence that is opened and never closed), the CLI shall report a DOCS-MD-001 finding naming the file and the fence's line, and exit 1.

When `--json` is given, the CLI shall print exactly one JSON document `{ pass, findings: [{ path, line, rule, message }] }` on standard output, with `pass` true and `findings` empty on a pass, and the same exit code as the text form.

If `docs check` is called without `--facts <dir>`, with an unknown argument, or with a <dir> that is missing or lacks a readable fact the check needs, then the CLI shall print a usage error naming the problem and exit 2.
While the control plane is not running, `sindri docs check --facts <dir>` shall run to completion in process and shall neither start serve nor contact it.
When step.docs.check runs in a workflow on the same facts, it shall produce the same findings (rule, path, line) as `sindri docs check --facts`, and keep its outcomes pass and fail (fact:findings).

When a changed markdown file links to a URL, a mail address, a bare #anchor or a directory, or holds a link inside a code fence, or a changed doc was deleted, the CLI shall continue to report no DOCS-LINK-001 or DOCS-MD-001 finding for it, as step.docs.check does today.

items.text: When `sindri docs check --facts <dir>` runs and the facts under <dir> describe a docs change whose paths are all doc paths, whose relative links all resolve and whose markdown all parses, the CLI shall print that the check passed and exit 0.
When the docs change under <dir> holds a path that is neither under the profile's doc globs nor a doc the design names, the CLI shall report a DOCS-PATH-001 finding for that path and exit 1.

When a changed markdown file has a relative link whose target does not exist in the workspace (or climbs out of the repo root), the CLI shall report a DOCS-LINK-001 finding naming the file, the link's line and the target, and exit 1.
When a changed markdown file does not parse (a code fence that is opened and never closed), the CLI shall report a DOCS-MD-001 finding naming the file and the fence's line, and exit 1.

When `--json` is given, the CLI shall print exactly one JSON document `{ pass, findings: [{ path, line, rule, message }] }` on standard output, with `pass` true and `findings` empty on a pass, and the same exit code as the text form.

If `docs check` is called without `--facts <dir>`, with an unknown argument, or with a <dir> that is missing or lacks a readable fact the check needs, then the CLI shall print a usage error naming the problem and exit 2.
While the control plane is not running, `sindri docs check --facts <dir>` shall run to completion in process and shall neither start serve nor contact it.
When step.docs.check runs in a workflow on the same facts, it shall produce the same findings (rule, path, line) as `sindri docs check --facts`, and keep its outcomes pass and fail (fact:findings).

When a changed markdown file links to a URL, a mail address, a bare #anchor or a directory, or holds a link inside a code fence, or a changed doc was deleted, the CLI shall continue to report no DOCS-LINK-001 or DOCS-MD-001 finding for it, as step.docs.check does today.

When <dir> is a run folder holding the facts as `docsScope` and `workspace` (named after the fact) or as `docsScope.json` and `workspace.json`, the CLI shall read them and run the check, so the call the step.docs.update seed makes (`sindri docs check --facts "$AW_SINDRI_RUN_DIR" --json`) works as written.
